title: Microsoft Teams: open, edit and discuss shared pages inside Teams
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and existing Loop controls are supported, and it does not infer a default or a new feature-specific switch. Minor corrections should acknowledge differences between Microsoft's permissions and Cloud Policy pages and cite the Copilot Pages policy reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let users open pages already shared in a Teams chat or channel inside Teams.
claims.quote: When someone shares a page in chat or a channel, you can open it in Teams, edit, and discuss with teammates.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the specific planned shared-page opening experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams shared pages open 580886; Pages in Teams opening shared pages license price default admin policy. Read Loop admin configuration, requirements and channel pages support; results describe existing integrations, not this roadmap experience.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default is unknown: Microsoft has not stated what this feature does on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams shared page open default Loop; Pages in Teams opening shared pages default admin policy. Read roadmap, channel pages support and Loop admin configuration. Existing Loop defaults are stated, but the new opening experience's default is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the new experience replaces today's browser or Loop app opening behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams shared page open default Loop; Teams opening pages policy. Read roadmap and channel pages support; Loop components ecosystem search excerpt describes browser links, but no text describes replacement by this planned experience.

claims.claim: The support article describes the channel pages as Loop pages.
claims.quote: In the Loop page you want to copy, select Share > Page link. ... Paste your Loop page link into the text box, and select Add page.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A user creates a channel page through the channel header's Add a tab > New page.
claims.quote: Find the channel you want to work in and select Add a tab in the channel header. Select New page.

claims.claim: Pages created through a channel are found in that channel's Shared tab.
claims.quote: You can find all pages created through a channel in that channel's Shared tab.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The support article says users with channel access can see and contribute to a created channel page.
claims.quote: Once a page is created or a Loop component is sent, all users who have access to the channel will be able to see and contribute to it.

claims.claim: The Loop admin page says components are always shared as editable, even when other files' default share links are view-only.
claims.quote: the components are always shared as editable by others, even if your organization is set to create shareable links that have view-only permissions as the default value for other file types.
claims.fix: After that sentence add: 'Microsoft's Loop permissions page also documents page and component sharing with edit or read-only access; the admin page's statement should not be read as granting every recipient edit access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/loop/loop-permission.

claims.claim: No source describes a change to existing sharing, permissions or storage for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams shared page open default Loop; Pages in Teams opening shared pages license price default admin policy. Read roadmap, channel pages support, Loop storage and permissions; no description of a new sharing, permission or storage mechanism was found.

claims.claim: Loop content is stored in OneDrive, SharePoint or SharePoint Embedded.
claims.quote: Loop content is stored in SharePoint, OneDrive, and SharePoint Embedded.

claims.claim: The channel support article locates channel pages in SharePoint for deletion.
claims.quote: To delete the content: 1. Locate the Loop page in SharePoint. 2. Hover over the item and select More options > Delete

claims.claim: Existing SharePoint retention rules govern Loop content stored in SharePoint.
claims.quote: When content is stored in SharePoint, the standard SharePoint IT policy is applied. Learn more about OneDrive and SharePoint Retention and Deletion.

claims.claim: Organizational sharing settings govern Loop page and component sharing.
claims.quote: Page and Component Sharing: Grants access to a specific page (not the whole workspace) with options for edit or read-only access. The user can choose to use a company share link or people-specific share link, based on your organizational sharing settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Loop creation controls do not restrict access to existing files or workspaces.
claims.quote: However, these admin controls don't restrict access to existing Loop files or workspaces.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Loop admin page points to Conditional Access to block access to existing Loop content.
claims.quote: To block access to existing Loop content or the Loop application, use Conditional Access policies.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -IsLoopEnabled $false is a SharePoint Online PowerShell call disabling Loop components in Teams.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell Module. ... -IsLoopEnabled ... Controls whether Loop components are available in Microsoft Teams. PARAMVALUE: True | False

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: IsLoopEnabled controls Teams Loop creation and integration tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This property controls Loop component creation and integration in Microsoft Teams. It applies to the entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: Teams Loop settings cannot be configured per user or scoped to a group for a pilot.
claims.quote: Admin controls can be applied to specific groups or the entire tenant, except for Teams-related settings, which always apply tenant-wide.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the Teams IsLoopEnabled control.
claims.quote: Searched: Loop IsLoopEnabled admin UI settings Teams creation SharePoint. Read Loop admin configuration and Set-SPOTenant; the Teams creation control is documented through SharePoint PowerShell, not an admin UI.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether IsLoopEnabled specifically governs the new shared-page opening experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Pages in Teams opening shared pages admin policy; Loop IsLoopEnabled admin UI settings Teams creation SharePoint. Read roadmap, channel support and Loop admin configuration; existing component integration is documented, not this new opening operation.

claims.claim: Loop workspace creation is configured in Microsoft 365 admin center > Home > Org settings > Services > Loop > Loop workspaces.
claims.quote: Navigate to Home > Org settings > Services > Loop. Choose your desired state for Loop workspaces via the checkbox.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator can change the admin center Loop setting.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center as Office Apps Administrator, Security Administrator, or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The admin center checkbox configures Create Loop workspaces in Loop for all users.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Admin Center configures the Cloud Policy setting Create Loop workspaces in Loop, described in the next section, targeted at All users (your full tenant).

claims.claim: Create Loop workspaces in Loop governs workspace creation including Teams channel workspaces.
claims.quote: Loop workspaces creation | Cloud Policy | Create Loop workspaces in Loop | Applies to: Loop workspaces, including Teams channel workspaces.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent is documented for setting Create Loop workspaces in Loop.
claims.quote: Searched: Create Loop workspaces in Loop Graph API PowerShell Cloud Policy; Cloud Policy Graph Loop configure policy API. Read Loop admin configuration, Cloud Policy overview and Set-SPOTenant reference; no operation setting this Cloud Policy was found.

claims.where: controls[2]; summary; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: No feature-specific switch for opening shared pages inside Teams is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Pages in Teams opening shared pages default admin policy; Teams opening pages policy; Loop IsLoopEnabled admin UI settings. Read roadmap, channel support, Loop admin configuration and Teams policies search excerpts; no feature-specific switch was found.

claims.claim: Get-SPOTenant without arguments retrieves the tenant state, including IsLoopEnabled.
claims.quote: To check if Loop components are enabled, run Get-SPOTenant without any arguments. Verify the value of IsLoopEnabled is true.

claims.claim: Get-SPOTenant requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: Microsoft says Loop components must be disabled in all tenant regions for consistent results.
claims.quote: If your organization has multiple regions (that is, organization URLs), you need to disable loop components for all the regions to have consistent results across the organization.

claims.claim: The Loop admin page gives config.office.com > Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > group > Configure Settings > Create Loop workspaces in Loop for group scoping.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list, choose either All users or select the group for which you want to apply the policy.
claims.fix: After the path add: 'The Cloud Policy overview describes selecting Add Groups on Choose the scope before Configure Settings: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy.' This acknowledges the different group-selection steps without invalidating the cited Loop route.

claims.claim: The Loop admin page says Teams creation and integration checks SharePoint properties, whereas channel workspace creation uses Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Teams creation and integration | SharePoint property | See Settings management for Loop components in Teams | Teams only checks the settings in this row.
